sentences.text: Once upon a time, there lived a very kind man named Hans.
He had a lovely garden where beautiful flowers grew in the sun.
His best friend was a rich man named Hugh.
The man often spoke nice words about true love and good work.
Hugh frequently visited the garden and took large amounts of fruit.
Hans never felt angry because he believed care was very important.
When winter came, poor Hans had a hard time with little food.
Hugh never visited his friend during those cold months.
Hans has always loved the sun and the flowers.
The cold weather made life difficult for poor Hans.
He stayed inside his small house during most of the winter days.
He had very little wood to keep a fire burning.
Sometimes he felt quite sad and lonely in the dark rooms.
He hoped that spring would return very soon to help him.
His friend Hugh sat in a warm room with plenty of food.
Hugh did not think about poor Hans at all during those weeks.
That made the winter even longer and harder for Hans.
He waited patiently for the warm sun to shine again.
Every day he looked out of his window at the white snow.
When spring finally arrived, the rich man came back to the garden.
He asked if Hans could give him his own broken car.
Hugh promised to give his old wood in return.
Hans agreed because he trusted his good friend completely.
Every day, the rich man gave Hans massive tasks around the farm.
One late evening, Hugh asked Hans to run for a doctor.
The man child had fallen off a horse.
Although Hans was very tired, he immediately started running through the storm.
Hans has always helped people when they need him.
He wanted to be a good friend to Hugh in every way.
The storm was very strong and the wind blew hard against his face.
He ran as fast as he could down the dark road.
Water covered the ground and made it difficult to see the path.
He thought about the child who needed help so much.
He did not want to stop for even a single minute.
His legs felt very heavy, but he continued to move forward.
The rain fell down upon him like cold tears from the sky.
He hoped the doctor would be ready to travel with him.
He knew that every second was important for the hurt child.
While Hans was running back, he lost his way in the dark.
He fell into a deep pool of water.
Because he was too tired, poor Hans sadly died.
At the gathering, the rich man cried about his best friend.
Then Hugh went straight back home to eat a big dinner.
If the man had cared, Hans would have lived.
Hans has given everything to his friend.
Now the story of poor Hans is finished.
People came together to remember the kind man who helped everyone.
They talked about how much they loved his beautiful flowers.
Hugh sat at the table and ate a very large meal.
He did not feel any real sadness in his heart.
He only pretended to cry in front of the other people.
The lovely garden remained empty without its kind owner there.
Nature went on just as before under the bright sun.
New flowers began to grow slowly in the warm ground.
Nobody forgot the story of Hans and his big heart.
His memory stayed alive in the hearts of the town people.
They learned a hard lesson about true friendship and care.
And so the sad tale of poor Hans came to an end.

sentences.text: Once upon a time, there lived a very kind little man whose name was Hans.
He had a lovely garden where beautiful flowers grew in the sun.
Although many people visited him, his best friend was a rich man named Hugh.
The man was so devoted to Hans that he always spoke nice words about true friendship.
Hugh often visited the garden and took large collections of flowers and fruit without paying anything.
Hans was so simple and good that he never felt angry about this.
He believed that friendship was the most important thing in the world.
However, when winter came, poor Hans had a hard time because he had no wood to burn and little food to eat.
Hugh never visited his poor friend during the cold winter months.
When spring finally arrived, Hugh came back to the garden.
He told Hans that he had an old cart which was broken.
Hugh asked if Hans could give him his own cart in exchange for the broken one.
Hans wanted to help, but he explained that his own cart was broken too.
The man, who expected everything for free, promised to give his old wood pieces to Hans.
In return, Hans had to carry a heavy package of bread and do a lot of hard work for Hugh.
Hans agreed because he trusted his devoted friend completely.
Every day, Hugh gave Hans massive tasks to finish around the big farm.
Hans was so tired that he could barely walk home at night.
One late evening, Hugh asked Hans to run into town to bring a doctor because his son had fallen off a horse.
Although Hans was exhausted, he immediately started running through the dark storm.
While Hans was running back from town, he lost his way in the dark and fell into a deep pool of water.
Because he was too tired to swim, poor Hans sadly died in the cold water.
At the ceremony, Hugh cried loudly and told everyone that he had lost his best friend.
After the sad event, Hugh went straight back to his comfortable home to eat a big dinner.
Hans was a man who loved his friend with all his heart.
He never thought that Hugh would treat him so badly.
If Hans had known the truth, he would not have agreed to work so hard.
The friendship which Hans valued so much was built on lies.
Hugh only wanted to take things from his kind neighbor without giving anything back.
When winter weather returned, Hans had suffered greatly in his little house.
The wood which he needed was kept by Hugh in a warm storage room.
If Hugh had been a true friend, he would have shared his wood and food with Hans.
Instead, Hugh let his friend freeze and go without food during the long months.
When spring came again, Hugh only thought about his own broken cart.
He wanted Hans to give him a good cart which could be used on the road.
Hans was always ready to give whatever he had to anyone who asked him.
That is why he accepted the bad trade proposed by the rich man.
He carried heavy packages and worked from morning until night without resting.
His muscles hurt, and his hands became rough from all the heavy labor.
Yet Hans remained happy because he believed in the beauty of friendship.
He did not know that Hugh was laughing behind his back.
The night when Hans ran through the storm was the last night of his life.
He ran as fast as he could because he wanted to save the doctor for the sick boy.
The wind blew strongly, and the rain fell heavily from the dark sky.
Hans could not see the deep pool of water where he finally met his terrible end.
If someone had helped Hans on the road, he might have survived the terrible storm.
No one was there to pull him out of the cold water.
The next morning, people found his body and brought the sad news to the village.
Hugh pretended to be very sad when he heard about the accident.
He told the people of the village that Hans was like a brother to him.
Then he walked home to enjoy his warm meal while his friend was gone forever.
True friendship means caring for others, but Hugh only cared for himself.

sentences.text: Once upon a time, there lived a very kind little man whose name was Hans.
He cultivated a lovely garden where beautiful flowers grew in the warm sun, a sanctuary of vibrant color and gentle fragrance.
Although many people visited him, his most devoted companion was a wealthy neighbor named Hugh.
The rich man frequently visited the garden, taking large collections of flowers and fruit without ever offering payment in return.
Hans was so simple and good-natured that he never felt a single spark of anger about this arrangement.
He firmly believed that true friendship was the most important thing in the world, transcending material wealth.
However, when winter arrived with its bitter frost, poor Hans had a remarkably hard time because he possessed no wood to burn and little food to eat.
During those freezing months, Hugh never once visited his struggling friend to check on his well-being.
When spring finally melted the snow, Hugh returned to the garden, carrying the casual air of someone who had never been away.
He informed Hans that he had an old cart which was broken, and asked if Hans could give him his own cart in exchange for the damaged one.
Hans wanted to help his companion, but he gently explained that his own cart was broken too, with a wheel that refused to turn.
The rich man, who always expected everything for free, promised to give his old wood pieces to Hans as a generous gesture.
In return, however, Hans had to carry a heavy package of bread into the village and perform a considerable amount of hard labor for Hugh.
Hans agreed to the terms without hesitation because he trusted his devoted friend completely.
He felt grateful that Hugh had remembered him after such a long and lonely winter.
Every single day, Hugh gave Hans massive tasks to finish around the big farm, testing the limits of his physical endurance.
Hans worked so strenuously from dawn until dusk that he could barely walk home along the dusty path at night.
One late evening, when the shadows had lengthened across the fields, Hugh hurried over with an urgent request.
He asked Hans to run into town immediately to fetch a doctor because his young son had fallen off a wild horse.
Although Hans was utterly exhausted from a day of heavy labor, he did not hesitate for a second.
He immediately started running through the deepening gloom as a heavy storm began to gather overhead.
The wind howled through the trees, whipping the rain across his face while he stumbled along the unfamiliar track.
While Hans was running back from town, desperately carrying the promise of medical help, he completely lost his way in the pitch-dark night.
In the blinding rain and darkness, he failed to see the danger lurking directly in front of him.
He stepped off the edge of the path and fell heavily into a deep pool of water.
Because he was far too tired to swim or even keep his head above the surface, poor Hans sadly drowned in the cold water.
The following morning, villagers discovered what remained of the kind little man and brought the devastating news to the surrounding area.
At the formal ceremony held in the village churchyard, Hugh cried loudly for all to see and told everyone that he had lost his very best friend.
He wiped away genuine-looking tears with a fine linen handkerchief while the neighbors nodded in sympathetic agreement.
After the sad event concluded, Hugh went straight back to his comfortable home to eat a large, satisfying dinner.
Hans had been a man who loved his friend with all his heart, never suspecting that Hugh would treat him with such utter disregard.
He never imagined for a moment that the wealthy neighbor would exploit his kindness for personal gain.
If Hans had known the harsh truth about Hugh's selfish nature, he would never have agreed to work so exhaustingly hard for scraps of wood.
The friendship which Hans valued so deeply was unfortunately built entirely upon deceit and convenience.
Hugh only wanted to take things from his kind neighbor without ever giving anything of real value back.
When the previous winter weather had returned, Hans had suffered greatly in his little house, shivering beneath thin blankets.
The heavy wood which he desperately needed to stay warm was kept locked away by Hugh in a dry, comfortable storage room.
If Hugh had truly been a loyal friend, he would surely have shared his abundant wood and surplus food with the freezing man.
Instead, Hugh comfortably let his faithful friend freeze and go without proper food during those long, cruel months.
When spring finally arrived again, Hugh thought of nothing except his own convenience and his broken cart.
He wanted Hans to hand over a sturdy, reliable cart which could be safely used on the main road for trade.
Hans was always ready to give whatever he had to anyone who asked him, possessing a heart incapable of refusal.
That is precisely why he accepted the terribly unfair trade proposed by the wealthy man without a single protest.
He carried heavy packages across the countryside and worked from morning until night without taking a proper rest.
His muscles ached constantly, and his hands became rough and calloused from all the heavy lifting.
Yet, remarkably, Hans remained cheerful because he believed so strongly in the idealized beauty of friendship.
He did not know that Hugh was laughing behind his back, mocking his simplicity among other wealthy landowners in the tavern.
The night when Hans ran through the violent storm was tragically the last night of his earthly life.
He had run as fast as his tired legs could carry him because he genuinely wanted to save the doctor for the injured boy.
The wind blew with terrible force, and the rain fell heavily from the black sky, hiding every landmark from view.
Hans could not see the deep pool of water where he finally met his terrible and lonely end.
If someone had happened to help Hans on the dark road, he might well have survived the terrifying storm.
No one was there to pull him out of the freezing water when he cried out in the darkness.
The next morning, people found his lifeless body in the pool and carried the tragic news back to the village.
Hugh pretended to be devastated by the accident, wiping his dry eyes before walking home to enjoy a warm meal while his friend was gone forever.
